where: Worked example 1, step 5 and dry run
problem: Step 5 computes 2(0.9821) − 1 = 0.9642 from the table, then quotes 0.9643 as the exact area. The dry-run row labelled '2Φ(2.1) − 1' shows 0.9643, mixing the table value with the exact value and inviting the student to think the table gives 0.9643.
fix: Keep the row as the table value 0.9642 and add a separate row 'exact 2Φ(2.1) − 1 = 0.9643', so the 0.0001 table rounding is visible as a difference.

problem: 'which keeps the mean about two standard deviations from both ends' implies the two end distances are similar. The distance from the mean to the far end in standard units is √(n(1−p)/p), which with p = 0.05 and n = 100 is about 44 standard deviations, not about two.
fix: Write 'which keeps the mean at least about two standard deviations away from each end of the range 0 to n' — the near end is about √5 ≈ 2.2 standard deviations away in the worst case.
